title: The token bucket
prompt:
Implement `TokenBucket(rate, capacity)` with `allow(now)`:

- refills `rate` tokens per second of elapsed time, capped at `capacity` (first call initializes the clock without refilling)
- a request succeeds iff at least 1 full token is available; it consumes exactly 1
- `now` is a float timestamp — never call time functions yourself (the bucket must be deterministic)

Burst of `capacity` at t=0 passes instantly; sustained throughput never exceeds `rate` per second.

tests.name: burst then throttle
tests.code:
b = TokenBucket(rate=2, capacity=5)
assert [b.allow(0.0) for _ in range(5)] == [True] * 5
assert b.allow(0.0) is False
assert b.allow(0.4) is False   # only 0.8 tokens accrued
assert b.allow(0.5) is True    # 1.0 tokens accrued
print('ok')
tests.hint: Refill = elapsed * rate, capped at capacity; spend whole tokens only.

tests.name: sustained rate holds
tests.code:
b = TokenBucket(rate=10, capacity=1)
allowed = sum(b.allow(t / 100) for t in range(100))
assert allowed == 10, allowed
print('ok')
tests.hint: One token per 0.1s — 100 ticks of 0.01s yield exactly 10.
